cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your parents' gravy needs stirring and you need a lift. Choose which job I'm doing; sauce doesn't pause politely when I leave.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you put dinner on a timer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A timer measures time. It does not stir. Gravy or station, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Gravy. I'll get a taxi. Just bring my suitcase downstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose again: suitcase or smooth gravy. I need one instruction that doesn't require me to leave the other one unattended.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 continuous sauce work, A3 timer correction and A5 unattended-task objection use A cooking competence to force explicit priorities.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 automation suggestion causes A3 stir/time distinction; B4 taxi solution adds suitcase, causing A5 renewed choice.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 try to solve the conflict rather than ask arbitrary questions; A identifies remaining demands.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes B4 practical taxi solution produce a new specific conflict with the same gravy obligation.

specificity.evidence: A1 parents gravy and lift, A3 station and B4 luggage make both duties immediate and ordinary.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 clipped timer correction is playable professional strain; A5 asks a precise usable instruction.
